ai_summary: Great Britain's wind generation currently stands at 10.7 GW, with Scotland contributing an estimated 4.1 GW, representing 40.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an ultra-clean carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, the wider GB grid records 67 gCO2/kWh, underscoring severe cross-border transmission bottlenecks that prevent clean energy from flowing south. Because the network cannot accommodate this abundant generation, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 19.9 GWh through Balancing Mechanism turn-down bids, incurring a direct constraint cost of about £1,129,884. To replace this lost zero-carbon electricity, thermal plants elsewhere on the network have burned an estimated 3,772,583 m3 of natural gas, releasing an avoidable 6,950 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing this daily constraint expenditure indicates an estimated total yearly cost of £412 million, which increases everybody's electricity invoice in the UK by approximately £1.5/MWh via balancing network charges. Accelerating grid reinforcement between Scotland and major English demand centres remains critical to stop paying generators to switch off while gas plants run elsewhere.
